text:
sre-bot: ALERT: dedicated-pool 'dedicated-gamma' tail_token_latency_p99 jumped 120ms -> 420ms in last 10m. noisy_neighbor_score=0.67. KV_cache_hit_rate dropped. auto-routing fallback events=8.
Elaine: I see the same on the per-pool view: https://console.redwood/pools/dedicated-gamma — kernel_select changed to 'auto-v2' around 1855002000. Coincides with the spike.
Raj: grabbing CPU/GPU profiler dumps now. suspect kernel switch + batch heuristics interacting with KV behavior. will post traces.
Luca: From infra snapshot: batch_timeout_ms was increased from 8 -> 20ms in the autoscale policy at ~1855001800 to tolerate noisy short bursts. That could increase in-flight tokens and worsen tail.
Maria: KV cache heatmap shows a quieting of hot-prefixes — hit_rate 0.92 -> 0.41 across that pool in 7m. Could be eviction churn due to larger batch windows.
Raj: posting mini pprof (truncated):
```
# pprof: token_serving_handler
CPU: 4 cores
samples: 1200
flat  cumulative   function
0.25s  1.80s       kv_cache::lookup
0.15s  0.60s       kernel_selector::score_candidate
0.60s  2.10s       runtime::dispatch_batch
```
Luca: interesting — kernel_selector is doing heavier scoring on 'auto-v2' (model feature checks + fallback checks). That adds ~150-300us per request at our QPS, multiplied by batch size.
Elaine: also note continuous batching increased average batch size from 6 -> 18 (per-pool telemetry). More queueing latency.
OpsMike: putting an emergency mitigation in flight: 1) pin kernel_select=kernel-stable-v1 for pool dedicated-gamma 2) reduce batch_timeout_ms to 6ms 3) disable aggressive KV eviction tweak. rolling to one node first.
Maria: can we get a quick panel on the Dedicated dashboard for 'token-level latency breakdown (queue | kernel | postprocess)' per-route? Right now per-route KPI is only mean latency. We need histograms.
Raj: query for new panel (PromQL-ish):
```
sum(rate(token_processing_time_seconds_bucket{pool="dedicated-gamma"}[1m])) by (le,route)
```
and
```
avg_over_time(kv_cache_hit_rate{pool="dedicated-gamma"}[5m])
```
Luca: suggest adding a noisy-neighbor fingerprint panel: correlates per-host GPU_util_pct vs pool_p99_delta and kernel_switch_events. Simple scatter and timeseries overlay will highlight spikes.
Elaine: after OpsMike's change, we should watch: tail_token_latency_p99, kv_cache_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, kernel_switch_count.
OpsMike: rollback/pin started on node-3 at 1855004400. patch id: ops/1855/mit-1. monitoring: https://console.redwood/pools/dedicated-gamma?live=true
Raj: I'll collect two more pprofs after the pin, and run a microbenchmark to isolate kernel selector cost with batch sizes 4/8/16.
Maria: I'll add the token-breakdown histogram to the dedicated-pools dashboard and a per-route filter (ETA ~ 30m). will also add an alert if kv_cache_hit_rate < 0.6 and tail_token_latency_p99 > 200ms.
Luca: long term: we should instrument kernel_selector internal timings and expose per-candidate cost metric, plus make kernel scoring async to avoid blocking hot paths. Filed RFC: https://go.redwood/rfcs/kernel-async-1855
Elaine: thumbs up. Keep comms in this thread. If tail doesn't improve in 10m, escalate and expand rollback.
OpsMike: current readouts (1855004560): tail_p99=180ms (was 420), kv_hit=0.63 (was 0.41), avg_batch=9 (was 18). partial improvement after pin. continuing rollouts to remaining nodes.
Raj: uploading traces + flamegraphs to the thread artifact store.
Elaine: thanks all — follow-up action items: OpsMike run full pool pin + batch timeout change; Maria add dashboard panels + alert; Raj collect and post traces; Luca draft kernel async RFC.
OpsMike: ack.
